newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia bank governor expects stable kuna, prices.
newsitem.headline: Croatia bank governor expects stable kuna, prices.

text.p: Croatia's central bank governor said on Friday he expected the country's kuna currency and prices to remain stable in 1997, with inflation hovering between 3.0 and 4.0 percent, state television (HRT) reported.

"1997 will be the year of stability...There is no reason why prices should rise quicker than they did last year. We expect inflation not higher than 3-4 percent," governor Marko Skreb told the HRT. Average inflation, according to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) estimates, would be 3.5 percent in 1996, in line with official forecasts and up from 1.6 percent in 1995.
The government launched a radical economic austerity programme in October 1993, when monthly inflation hit 38.7 percent. Kuna was introduced in spring 1994.
Skreb also said kuna would rank as one of most stable currencies in Europe in 1996.
"We'll be the country with a most stable currency not only among the countries in transition, but will be near the top in Europe as well," he said.
Kuna hovered around just under 3.6 to the German mark and around 5.5 versus the dollar this year.
At the time it was introduced its exchange rate was around 3.7 to the mark and around 6.0 to the dollar.
Skreb listed introduction of kuna in the country's last Serb-held enclave as the top short-term priority of 1997 financial policy.
Croatian government is to take control over the enclave of Eastern Slavonia before summer.
National Bank of Croatia has some $2.3 billion foreign currency reserves, "enough to defend the currency against any speculations," as the country opens to foreign investments, Skreb said.
Commercial banks also hold 2.1 foreign currency reserves, he added.
Skreb was confident his forecasts were right.
"If (my forecasts) prove to be wrong, be sure the bank will undertake adequate measures," he told the HRT.
"If this is not enough, I believe I won't see the end of 1997 in my present post."
